title: An island nest
hook: A new visitor can add a new interaction.

knows: Animals depend on features of their surroundings.
doesNotKnow: In a toy island scenario, a newly introduced predator can reach ground nests and eat eggs. Which direct risk is added?

misconception: A single observation or change determines the same outcome everywhere.
objective: In a toy island scenario, a newly introduced predator can reach ground nests and eat eggs. Which direct risk is added?

claims.text: In a toy island scenario, a newly introduced predator can reach ground nests and eat eggs. Which direct risk is added? The first panel shows a ground nest; the second adds a stipulated predator with access to it. Egg predation is an added possible risk in this toy example. The diagram is not an observed island or a prediction that every nest will be lost.
claims.source: Stipulated illustrative scenario, not wildlife observations. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, ecology, https://openstax.org/details/books/biology-2e

claims.text: The panels show a simplified illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
In a toy habitat a new predator reaches nests on the ground. What might be directly at risk? If a predator can reach and eat eggs, the accessible eggs are at risk.
